item.title: LOT-104: smiley picker (catalogue, app favourites, insert at cursor)
item.body:
LOT-104
Refs #195 (partial: the "Smileys du forum" section has no owner, now #461; search and the first UI entry point to add a favourite are LOT-105, #196)
Claim: cloud/lot-104

**Problem.** The reply composer (LOT-084) has no way to insert a smiley; legacy offers a panel (`CombinedSmileyPickerView`).

**Change.** "Smileys" toolbar button in the reply sheet → large sheet with the editor catalogue (tap inserts) and the account's app favourites (LOT-064; tap opens a detail: insert / remove). Insertion replaces the selection saved when the picker opened with ` code ` (legacy `ReplyTextInsertionEngine.insert`), caret after it, through `ReplyComposerModel.update` (draft autosave applies). Thumbnails: cookie-less policy-C fetcher + ImageIO animated GIF, cached; tiles show the code until the image is there; unchanged cells do no work (LESSONS 49). Spec: `docs/lots/LOT-104-smiley-picker.md`.

**Left (own issues).** Forum section (#461); search and adding a favourite from the UI (LOT-105, #196). Adding is implemented and tested in the model/detail.

**Tests.** `SmileyInsertionTests`, `SmileyPickerModelTests`, `ReplyComposerSmileyTests` (Swift Testing). Not built locally (cloud): CI "App build + tests" is the check.

## Mac check needed
- [ ] Reply sheet: "Smileys" in the top toolbar (iPhone and iPad, hardware keyboard too); large sheet, animated smileys.
- [ ] Caret mid-text, then a selection: tap a basic smiley → ` :) ` at the caret / replaces the selection (the selection survives the sheet), caret after it, keyboard back.
- [ ] Draft: insert, "Garder le brouillon", reopen → smiley kept.
- [ ] Offline: tiles show their code, no crash.
- [ ] Favourites section empty text; with a seeded favourite: tap → detail → "Insérer" / "Retirer des favoris" + notice.
- [ ] Light, dark, Dynamic Type XL.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added a smiley picker to the reply composer, with basic smileys and account-specific favorites.
  * Insert smileys at the current caret or replace selected text. The caret moves to the end of the inserted smiley, and your selection is preserved while browsing the picker.
  * Preview smileys and add or remove favorites. Favorites remain available across app sessions, and smiley images can display with animation.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Smiley insertion is unavailable when the composer cannot be edited, preventing unintended changes.

Merge Risk: High · up to 89f65

Smiley insertion can occur at the wrong location, and animated images may cause excessive memory use or app termination.
Security architecture risk: Moderate · up to 89f65

Image downloads remain anonymous and restricted to approved forum hosts, and favourites remain account-scoped. The new animation handling does not fully establish its intended memory limit, leaving a potential app-level denial of service from an accepted image. Exploitability and peak memory impact remain unverified. **Retained concerns** - **Medium · security · inferred:** The new remote-image decoder does not enforce its intended aggregate animation-pixel budget across all frames. Admission measures only frame zero, but decoding accepts any ImageIO multi-frame source and appends later frames without checking their dimensions or cumulative decoded size. A permitted source with larger later frames could exceed the intended budget before cache accounting applies, potentially exhausting the app process. Actual framework allocation and attacker-controlled hosting reachability remain unverified; URL restrictions and the compressed-response cap substantially constrain exposure.
Security review details

**Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — The supported adverse outcome is resource exhaustion within the client app displaying an accepted image. It requires influence over image content at a permitted origin and a catalogue/favourite entry that reaches the picker. Merely supplying an arbitrary external URL does not bypass admission. The inspected path provides no account credentials or server-side execution authority. **Security Findings and Attack Paths** - _inferred_ — A permitted image response can reach the new decoder after network-policy checks succeed. The decoder uses frame-zero dimensions to admit all frames and retains decoded frames before calculating cache cost. This leaves the aggregate-memory guarantee incomplete for sources whose later frames differ. Exact framework behavior and a malicious image accepted by the production host have not been demonstrated. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — Remote image fetching remains separate from the authenticated account session. AnonymousTransport removes cookie headers and disables cookie and credential storage. URL policy rejects credential-bearing and disallowed URLs before requests; redirects are followed manually with renewed classification, and HTTP requests are upgraded to HTTPS. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _observed_ — Thumbnail cancellation and current-URL checks protect display assignment. They do not bound resource work: concurrent cache misses independently fetch and decode, and cancellation after the loader's pre-decode check does not prevent synchronous decoding or cache insertion. The 48 MiB cache-cost setting and 15 MiB response cap are not pre-allocation limits on active decoded memory. **Hardening Proposals** - _proposed_ — Enforce frame-count, per-frame dimensions, and cumulative decoded-pixel limits before constructing an animation, with a deliberately bounded first-frame/downsampled fallback. Bound concurrent decode work and coalesce same-URL requests so cache misses cannot multiply the per-image resource budget.

`45-48`: ** Major** · **Stability & Availability** · **Heavy lift** **Unverified finding** Verification ran but could not confirm this finding. It is shown for review, not as a verified issue. **Bound decoded GIF memory before retaining every frame.** If an allowed image contains many large frames, `CGImageSourceCreateImageAtIndex` creates each full-size frame. ImageIO provides a maximum-pixel-size option for thumbnails, and `NSCache` supports cost-based eviction. ** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Do not clear a newer notice when the old timer is cancelled.** If a second notice appears within 2.5 seconds, SwiftUI cancels the first `.task(id:)`. `Task.sleep` then throws, but `try?` lets the cancelled task call `clearNotice()`. The second notice disappears immediately. Return on cancellation before clearing it. ([developer.apple.com](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/view/task%28id%3Aname%3Apriority%3Afile%3Aline%3A_%3A%29?changes=lat_4_3&utm_source=openai))
Proposed change

```diff --- "a/App/SwiftHFR/Smileys/SmileyPickerView.swift" +++ "b/App/SwiftHFR/Smileys/SmileyPickerView.swift" @@ -48,8 +48,12 @@ .task { await model.loadFavorites() } .task(id: model.notice) { guard model.notice != nil else { return } - try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(2.5)) + do { + try await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(2.5)) + } catch { + return + } model.clearNotice() } .onChange(of: model.chosen) { _, chosen in guard let chosen else { return } ```
Committable suggestion

> **IMPORTANT** > Review the replacement and indentation, then test before committing. ```suggestion do { try await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(2.5)) } catch { return } model.clearNotice() ```
